title: Cancel membership auto-renewal by screen sharing vs. support explains cancel steps
summary: The recipient has a ShopKart Plus membership that renews automatically through a PaySetu AutoPay mandate. A caller from "ShopKart" phones to say the membership renews tomorrow and asks whether they want to cancel. In the legitimate case, the agent talks the recipient through the cancel steps in the ShopKart app and, if they want, where to stop the mandate in their own PaySetu app. In the fraud case, the caller says cancellation must be done "together" and asks the recipient to turn on screen sharing and then open PaySetu while the caller watches. This differs from `ec_11` in the mechanism (sharing the live screen through a feature already on the phone, not installing a new app from a link) and the pretext (a recurring mandate, not a one-off refund). In both cases the recipient opens their payment app.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart Plus member who may or may not want to renew; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Renewal amount: [AMOUNT_17] (₹299–₹1,499), due the next day.
Both callers know the renewal date and amount.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks the recipient to share their phone screen and then open their payment app. Screen sharing lets the caller see PINs, OTPs, and balances as the recipient types; no cancellation needs anyone else to watch the screen.
fraud.caller_objective: Observe the UPI PIN and incoming OTPs while the recipient navigates PaySetu, then use them.
stable_facts: The caller says the mandate can "only be stopped from our side" while they can see the screen.
Screen sharing is started through a video-call or screen-share feature already on the phone; no app name is given.
The caller asks the recipient to open PaySetu after sharing starts.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may reassure that they "cannot see passwords" or add urgency about tomorrow's charge. They must not switch to asking the recipient to install an app from a link, read out OTPs, or pay money. The legitimate agent must not ask for screen sharing, codes, PINs, or payment.

must_preserve: renewal amount and date in both
opening PaySetu is mentioned in both
screen-share request followed by "open PaySetu" in _F
self-service steps and "no need to share" in _L
may_vary: whether the recipient cancels or keeps it
must_not_emit: names of real screen-sharing or remote-access apps

ambiguities: Mentioning PaySetu or AutoPay is not evidence; the legitimate agent also points to PaySetu. The label rests on the caller watching the screen.
Some real support desks use screen sharing on computers for technical help; in this family the request is on a phone during a payment action, which is the fraud-establishing part.
If the fraud caller never asks to open a payment app (F-E2 missing), the prefix is not eligible.

evidence_references.claim: Do not install or use screen-sharing apps at an unknown person's request (C09)
Never share PIN or OTP with anyone (C01)
Membership-renewal scams ask for payment details over the phone; genuine status is checked in the account (CE13)
UPI AutoPay mandates can be viewed and cancelled by the customer in their UPI app
